messages:
sam: Quick follow-up on the rollout metadata RFC. I sketched a slimmer shape that keeps pin semantics in control-plane and gives clients ordered fallbacks + a tiny epoch counter. Want quick takes before I add it to the appendix.

anya: Can you drop the example here? Need to see fields we expect runtime to read.

sam: Pasted below. Main goals: (1) clients can pick a candidate quickly, (2) runtime gets fast hints, (3) control-plane can rotate order without confusing cached clients.

```json
{
  "artifact": "auth-encoder-4b",
  "stamp": "v2026-03-22",
  "stamp_seq": 7,
  "stamp_fingerprint": "sha256:deadbeef...",
  "candidates": [
    {"type":"hash","id":"sha256:aa11","variant":"fp16","priority":0},
    {"type":"stamp","id":"v2026-03-21","variant":"int8","priority":1}
  ],
  "fallback_policy":"ordered",
  "soft_expiry":"2026-07-01T00:00:00Z",
  "stamp_origin":"canary",
  "preferred_seq_len":512,
  "runtime_annotations":["placement:short-seq"],
  "client_hints":{"preferred_seq_len":512,"cost_bucket":"medium"}
}
```

sam: Key differences from previous drafts: added `stamp_fingerprint` (authoritative mapping to immutable content), `stamp_seq` for cache invalidation, and typed candidate ids to avoid guessing. Also `preferred_seq_len` duplicated at top-level for fast path.

rui: +1 on stamp_seq. A few concerns: if we republish the same `stamp` but increment `stamp_seq`, do clients always re-resolve or do we need a TTL bump? We should be explicit about cache semantics.

anya: For cache semantics let's do: clients must compare local `stamp_seq` and re-resolve if control-plane seq > local. If equal, safe to reuse. Add guidance for a short network TTL for stamp lookups.

rui: Also suggest `stamp_fingerprint` required when `candidates` include hashes. That prevents silent remapping of a stamp to completely different content without visibility. Control-plane can still allow mapping changes but we alert on fingerprint diffs.

sam: Good. I don't want to block changes automatically; operator alerts are enough. We'll add a control-plane health check that surfaces "stamp -> fingerprint mismatch" as warning.

devops-bot: schema-check: staging failed: field `client_hints.cost_bucket` typed as string while production schema expected enum; ticket INF-2201 created.

anya: Hmm, we should standardize client_hints types so they don't break schema validators. Either make client_hints opaque map (string-only) or enforce types at control-plane ingestion. I'd vote enforce on ingest and normalize.

rui: Tenant overrides: Dedicated customers may require `hard_pin:true` semantics where control-plane must keep stamp -> fingerprint mapping immutable until tenant releases. We should document tenant_override behavior clearly.

sam: Agreed. We'll add `tenant_overrides` section in appendix describing `hard_pin` and `pin_ttl` semantics.

anya: Minor runtime note: duplication of `preferred_seq_len` top-level means storage consumers must prefer top-level if present. We'll add a single-line contract in the appendix.

devops-bot: INF-2201 tracked. Will re-run after schema change.

sam: Action items:
- sam: update appendix with `stamp_seq`, `stamp_fingerprint`, typed candidate ids, and tenant_override examples (ETA today).
- anya: write cache semantics blurb and TTL recommendation (ETA tomorrow).
- rui: add control-plane alert rule for fingerprint divergence and wire `hard_pin` semantics into billing/tenant profile (ETA 3 days).
- devops-bot: re-run schema tests once changes landed.

anya: fine by me. If no objections I'll merge the appendix after sam's edits. :+1:

sam: merging after small edits, will ping when deployed.

rui: thanks, this should make runtime behavior much clearer and keep clients simple.
